title: Introduce gradual decommitment retainer and utilization-delta reporter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a short-window decommit retention mechanism for Dedicated fleets to reduce churn during transient drops, plus a new utilization-delta reporter metric stream and Console dashboard tiles. Default off; opt-in via feature flag. No API contract changes.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets see frequent brief utilization drops (seconds->minutes) that trigger decommits and warmup thrash for certain tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight 'decommitment retainer' that holds recently-freed slots in a soft-retained state for a configurable short window (default 120s). If a tenant or pool re-requests capacity within the window, the retainer allows immediate reuse instead of a full reprovision. To observe the feature impact and simplify autoscaler tuning, this change also adds a utilization-delta reporter that emits per-pool and per-tenant utilization deltas across multiple windows (10s, 60s, 300s).

What this PR changes (high level):
- Implement core retainer: retention lifecycle, reclaim policy, and metrics (retained_slots_total, retained_slots_hit_count, retained_slot_age_seconds_histogram).
- Autoscaler integration: optional tightening/relaxing hooks where the autoscaler consults retained_capacity() to avoid aggressive decommits during transient dips.
- Utilization-delta reporter: sidecar component in fleet-controller that computes delta-series and exports prometheus-friendly counters and an aggregated HDR sketch for latency-targeted analysis.
- Console additions: two new tiles under Dedicated Fleet -> Utilization: "Retention hit rate" and "Utilization deltas (10s/60s/5m)" (feature-flag gated).
- Config: cluster-level feature flag dedicated.decommit_retention.enabled and per-pool retention_window_seconds; safe defaults keep feature off in production until rollout.

Implementation notes:
- Retainer is implemented as a small in-memory, eviction-aware structure persisted to the cluster state directory to survive controller restarts for short windows. It does not alter lease semantics; it only short-circuits the cold-provision path when reclaiming. The component exposes a clear metrics surface to evaluate value before making it the default behaviour.
- Utilization-delta reporter computes deltas using sliding windows and samples at controller tick; it keeps a rolling reservoir to bound memory usage and emits both raw counters and HDR sketches for percentiles.
- We intentionally avoided changing warm-pool reconciliation logic; retainer acts as a fast-path read for request admission. If warm-pools are enabled, they continue to operate and retainer is complementary.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (off by default).
2) Canary enable in a single test cluster for 24 hours with debug metrics retention; review retained_slots_hit_count and warmup latency.
3) Gradual enable for 5% of Dedicated tenants using the feature gating service; monitor autoscaler oscillation and tenant SLOs.
4) If stable after 72 hours of production telemetry, increase to 100% and promote Console tiles to general availability.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for retention lifecycle, eviction, and reclaim decisioning.
- Integration test simulating transient surge/decommit scenarios showing ~35-50% reduction in reprovision events for the test workload.
- Load test on perf-canary cluster with 10k small requests to ensure memory/CPU overhead of reporter is <2%.
- E2E smoke in staging with Console tiles validated.

Known limitations and future work:
- Currently retention is per-slot; future work will add affinity-aware retention (maintain slot locality for tenant affinity).
- Persistent backing is intentionally lightweight; long restarts beyond retention_window_seconds will naturally evict entries.
- Reporter currently uses a single sampling frequency; we may expose dynamic sampling for high-cardinality tenants.

feat(telemetry): introduce utilization-delta reporter and HDR sketch exporter (Aisha Patel)
perf(autoscale): consult retained capacity before decommit decisions (Lina Zhang)
docs: add Console tile descriptions and rollout playbook (Omar Reyes)
test: integration + load tests for retainer and reporter (Ben Thompson)
review_comments: Ben Thompson: Nice incremental approach. Two asks: (1) add a timeout jitter to retention_window_seconds to avoid synchronized reclaims; (2) include a per-tenant max_retained_slots cap — otherwise noisy tenants could hold resources.
Aisha Patel: Addressed both. Added jitter delta +-10% by default and per-pool max_retained_slots with 0=unbounded. Documented behavior in defaults.yaml.
Lina Zhang: Observability looks good. Please ensure the HDR sketch buckets are bounded when cardinality spikes. Also run the perf test with retained_slots hit enabled.
Aisha Patel: Bounded reservoir added (configurable 1000 samples). Perf tests updated and results included in PR description.
Omar Reyes: Consider gating Console tiles behind the same feature flag so we don't surface metrics for disabled clusters.
Aisha Patel: Done — UI respects dedicated.decommit_retention.enabled before rendering tiles.
Ben Thompson: Approving after small nits fixed (comments inline about log levels).

notes: Feature is off by default. Operations to canary are documented in docs/engineering/dedicated/retainer.md.
